Message:
From the peaks of Mount Yuhtunga to the ocean floors of the Bastore Sea, I daresay there are none more deserving of renown than she, filling our hearts with admiration and fear in equal measure.

That selfsame admiration is why I volunteered to go and interview her on behalf of “*Magic Paradise Weekly*”, but fear halted my steps. Indeed, it was all I could do to observe her from a distance.

I thought I remained an unseen witness to her wonders and horrors, but who else could have placed that curse on me? Who else could have lifted it?

This beautifully carved ornament is covered in glowing inscriptions, each symbol strange and unintelligible. Several arcane diagrams accompany the text, implying the tablet harbors some kind of enchantment or incantation, but without a means of deciphering it, you can but hypothesize about its use.
The display case is filled with lustrous minerals, their dense aetheric signature reminiscent of the crystals used to power familiars. Perhaps they were used as such during the Fifth Astral Era?

You cast your eyes over the array of gleaming equipment, including what appears to be a cane and some bracelets. On closer inspection, each artifact is carved with intricate patterns that bespeak their occult nature. These were likely crafted during the War of the Magi, when the practice of imbuing arms and armor with arcane properties was at its zenith.

A collection of intricately carved circular sigils line the wall. Judging by the arcane patterns that adorn them, the discs would likely react to an influx of aether. Given the highly dangerous nature of the knowledge stored within these walls, however, you decide not to put that theory to the test...

There appears to be no unifying characteristic among the bones and fossils on display─save for the vague sense of unease you feel examining each specimen. What strange, warped beasts could these relics originate from?
